checks.name: Strong enough to be real
checks.why: Is the dip clearly above the noise, or could random scatter make it?

checks.name: Repeats on schedule
checks.why: A planet dims its star at a perfectly regular interval.

checks.name: Not one glitch
checks.why: A single bad data point or satellite momentum dump can fake a 'periodic' signal.

checks.name: Odd = even depths
checks.why: Two stars eclipsing each other often make alternating deep/shallow dips.

checks.name: No secondary eclipse
checks.why: Planets are dark; a second dip halfway through the orbit means a glowing companion star.

checks.name: Flat-bottomed shape
checks.why: A planet fully crossing the star gives a U-shaped dip; grazing binaries are V-shaped.

checks.name: Planet-sized
checks.why: Anything much bigger than Jupiter is a star, not a planet.

checks.name: Duration fits the star
checks.why: Kepler's laws predict how long a transit should last for this star and period.
